name: AWS (Amazon Web Services)
tagline: World's largest cloud: compute, storage, databases, custom chips and Bedrock AI

strategy.label: Mission
strategy.text: Be Earth's most customer-centric cloud: give builders of every size the broadest, deepest set of on-demand IT primitives.

strategy.label: Vision
strategy.text: Every application and AI agent runs on AWS; Jassy calls it a potential $1 trillion revenue business.

strategy.label: Core strategy
strategy.text: Primitives over solutions: 200+ services, pay-as-you-go, relentless price cuts, then layer Bedrock and agents on top.

strategy.label: Moat
strategy.text: Largest installed base and partner ecosystem, operational reliability record, Graviton and Trainium silicon lowering cost per workload.

strategy.label: Key bet
strategy.text: Trainium plus model choice: Anthropic up to 5 GW, OpenAI ~2 GW from 2027; OpenAI models on Bedrock since Apr 2026.

strategy.label: Your view
strategy.text: AWS grew 37% but lost share to Google: is being model-neutral a moat, or proof it lacks a frontier model?

customers.who: Banks, retailers, telcos migrating from data centres
customers.pain: Legacy data centres slow, costly; need security, compliance, global reach
customers.why: Broadest services, mature security certifications, migration programs and largest SI partner network

customers.pain: Need to scale fast without upfront hardware capex
customers.why: Credits via Activate, pay-as-you-go, default choice of most engineers

customers.who: Anthropic, OpenAI, model and agent startups
customers.pain: GPU scarcity and soaring training and inference cost
customers.why: Trainium price-performance, gigawatt-scale capacity, Bedrock distribution to enterprise buyers

customers.pain: Data sovereignty, classified workloads, strict residency rules
customers.why: GovCloud, sovereign cloud offerings, local regions in India and EU

customers.pain: Need a channel to reach cloud budgets
customers.why: AWS Marketplace lets customers burn committed spend on partner software

products.name: EC2
products.desc: Virtual servers incl. Graviton CPUs and Nvidia GPU instances

products.name: S3
products.desc: Object storage, backbone of data lakes

portfolio.north_star: Compute hours consumed by active production workloads
portfolio.key_metrics: Revenue growth, backlog, net revenue retention, utilisation, cost per instance-hour
portfolio.guardrails: Availability SLAs, major outage count, security incidents, customer bill shock

products.name: Amazon Bedrock
products.desc: Managed access to Claude, GPT, Nova, Llama and more

products.name: Trainium / Inferentia
products.desc: Custom AI chips; Trainium sold out through 2027

products.name: SageMaker
products.desc: Build, train and deploy ML models

products.name: Bedrock AgentCore
products.desc: Runtime, memory and identity for production AI agents

portfolio.north_star: Inference tokens served on AWS for paying production workloads
portfolio.key_metrics: AI run-rate (~$25B), Trainium share of capacity, Bedrock active customers
portfolio.guardrails: Model latency, capacity wait times, gross margin per GW deployed

products.name: Amazon Quick
products.desc: AI assistant for work with desktop app and agents

products.name: Amazon Connect
products.desc: AI contact centre, now hiring and supply-chain agents

products.name: AWS Marketplace
products.desc: Buy third-party software against AWS commits

portfolio.north_star: Weekly active business users completing tasks with AWS apps
portfolio.key_metrics: Seats, WAU, Connect minutes, Marketplace GMV, attach to infra
portfolio.guardrails: Partner conflict, data privacy complaints, churn after free trials

rows.how: Per second, per GB; discounts via Savings Plans and reserved instances
Multi-year commits for discounts; builds $496B backlog
Per token, per accelerator hour, or provisioned throughput
Listing fee share; support priced as percentage of spend

bullets.label: Revenue mix
bullets.text: ~17-18% of Amazon revenue but well over half of operating income; AI run-rate ~$25B within $169B ARR.

bullets.label: Users vs payers
bullets.text: Engineers choose services; CIOs and CFOs sign commits; AI labs are now a few huge payers.

bullets.label: Unit economics
bullets.text: Op margin ~39% Q2 2026; depreciation from $220B capex and memory price spikes pressure future margins.

bullets.label: Growth levers
bullets.text: Convert $496B backlog as capacity lands, Trainium cost advantage, OpenAI on Bedrock, agents, sovereign regions.

bullets.label: Constraint
bullets.text: Power and chip supply, not demand, caps growth; capacity added faster is revenue recognised sooner.

friction: Complex, unpredictable bills; hard to forecast spend
200+ services with overlapping names confuse newcomers
Console UX dated versus newer developer platforms
GPU and Trainium capacity waitlists for AI workloads
High egress fees discourage multicloud architectures

competitors.label: Hyperscale
competitors.text: Microsoft Azure (~20%), Google Cloud (~15%), Oracle OCI

competitors.label: AI infra
competitors.text: CoreWeave, Nebius, Oracle for GPU capacity

competitors.label: India
competitors.text: Azure, Google Cloud, Jio-led cloud, Yotta, CtrlS sovereign clouds

competitors.label: Edge
competitors.text: Scale, reliability, custom silicon economics, and widest model choice

competitors.label: Risk
competitors.text: Share loss to rivals with own frontier models; concentration in Anthropic

news.label: Apr 2026
news.text: Azure exclusivity ends; OpenAI models, Codex arrive on Amazon Bedrock

news.label: Watch
news.text: Can capacity build keep pace? Trainium sales outside AWS; share versus Google
